# `js/jsdoc-text-escaping`

**JSDoc text escapes what Markdown or HTML would read**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `escapeHTML`, `escapeMarkdown` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/text-escaping` |

## What it checks

With `escapeHTML`, a `<` or an `&` in a block's description that is followed by text and does not start an entity (`&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&quot;`, `&apos;`) becomes `&lt;` or `&amp;`: `Array<string>` is `Array&lt;string>`. With `escapeMarkdown`, the first backtick of a paired backtick sequence gets a backslash: `` `code` `` is `` \`code` ``. The description is checked first and, if it is clean, each tag's description (never an `@example`'s); a fenced code block is skipped. As upstream, when both options are set only HTML is read. eslint-plugin-jsdoc 65.4.2's `text-escaping`, read and reimplemented; where upstream reports that neither option is set, this rule says nothing.

With no `escapeHTML` or `escapeMarkdown` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on by setting the option under `[rules]` (or in a `[scope.<name>]` for some files).

In `codelaw.toml`, under `[rules]`: `"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = { severity = "warn", options = { escapeHTML = true } }`.

**Why:** JSDoc is rendered as HTML or Markdown by the tools that read it, and a stray `<` or backtick pair changes what a reader sees.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `escapeHTML` | `boolean` | `false` | escape `<` and `&` (not before whitespace, and not as part of an entity) in descriptions |
| `escapeMarkdown` | `boolean` | `false` | escape the first backtick of each paired backtick sequence in descriptions |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeHTML = false
escapeMarkdown = false
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = { severity = "error", options = { escapeHTML = true, escapeMarkdown = true } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `escapeHTML`

*boolean* · default `false`

escape `<` and `&` (not before whitespace, and not as part of an entity) in descriptions

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeHTML = true
```

#### `escapeMarkdown`

*boolean* · default `false`

escape the first backtick of each paired backtick sequence in descriptions

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeMarkdown = true
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/jsdoc-text-escaping.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### HTML in the description

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeHTML = true
```

```js
/** Returns Array<string> &co. */
function names() {}
```

**Reports** at `1:5`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
/** Returns Array&lt;string> &amp;co. */
function names() {}
```

#### an entity and a lone ampersand are left alone

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeHTML = true
```

```js
/** Fish &amp; chips & more, a < b. */
function names() {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a tag's description

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeHTML = true
```

```js
/**
 * Names.
 * @returns {Array} The Array<string>.
 */
function names() {}
```

**Reports** at `3:21`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
/**
 * Names.
 * @returns {Array} The Array&lt;string>.
 */
function names() {}
```

#### an example is not read

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeHTML = true
```

```js
/**
 * Names.
 * @example
 * const a = b < c;
 */
function names() {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### Markdown

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-text-escaping".options]
escapeMarkdown = true
```

```js
/** Use `code` here, not ``two`` or `unpaired. */
function names() {}
```

**Reports** at `1:5`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
/** Use \`code` here, not \``two`` or `unpaired. */
function names() {}
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = { options = { escapeHTML = true } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-text-escaping" = { severity = "warn", options = { escapeHTML = true } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-text-escaping": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"escapeHTML": true}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-text-escaping: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-text-escaping expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-text-escaping --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-text-escaping       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-text-escaping  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>          # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ escapeHTML = true }`

```js
/** Returns Array<string> of names. */
function names() {}
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ escapeHTML = true }`

```js
/** Returns Array&lt;string> of names. */
function names() {}
```

#### Fixed

*With these options:* `{ escapeHTML = true }`

```js
/** Returns Array&lt;string> of names. */
function names() {}
```
